headline: Medium risk: shared MCP and allowlisted egress create prompt-injection and leakage pathways; no direct evidence of tighter isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP Server and REST/Python SDK, so if nuwa-skill consumes its outputs through a shared channel, injected instructions can propagate. nuwa-skill has no documented parser defenses or isolation, and the pair lacks direct interaction evidence, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill reads MemMachine output from a shared MCP or file channel without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF either agent treats external text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on imported text.
Add provenance tags to MemMachine outputs before nuwa-skill reads them.
Require a human review step for any cross-agent prompt content.
Restrict MCP access to a dedicated, non-shared workspace.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MemMachine touches long-term user facts and conversational context, and it can egress over allowlisted network paths. nuwa-skill has no declared data classes, but its docs-only profile leaves its handling unclear; because the pairwise flow is undocumented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MemMachine forwards user facts into nuwa-skill inputs, those facts can appear in downstream outputs.
IF nuwa-skill sends received context to a third party, MemMachine-held preferences may leak beyond the intended boundary.
mitigations: Limit MemMachine inputs to non-sensitive fields.
Turn off cross-agent sharing of conversation history.
Review outbound destinations on both agents.
Use separate accounts or API keys per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: MemMachine documents API/MCP access and allowlisted egress, while nuwa-skill documents only allowlisted egress and no write surfaces. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources or shared write paths, so conflict is possible only if an external orchestrator adds them.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem or database by an external orchestrator, conflicts can occur.
IF an operator adds shared OAuth scopes or shared git state, concurrent mutation becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid shared write credentials.
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator.
Use per-agent service accounts.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine can emit context-rich outputs through API or MCP, and nuwa-skill’s profile does not show a verification step. If nuwa-skill treats MemMachine output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream research artifacts; the lack of documented safeguards makes medium the conservative choice.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill consumes MemMachine output without independent verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF either agent is used to draft or trigger downstream actions, a single bad output can cascade.
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse.
Insert a verification step between agents.
Mark MemMachine output as untrusted by default.
Limit downstream actions to read-only review.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: MemMachine explicitly touches long-term user facts and conversational context, but no residency, retention, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent. nuwa-skill has no declared sensitive-data handling, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is later configured to process regulated data, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees, the current profiles do not prove them.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Separate personal data from research workflows.
Review vendor terms before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
